clue.text: He wrote for various papers

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the word that follows appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A journalist who freelanced for several newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges PAPERS. Sapper was the pen name of H. C. McNeile, the British author of the Bulldog Drummond thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name belonged to a novelist, so this man is someone who wrote books.

clue.text: A patient compilation

parts.note: read as a compiled list of people who are patients, those off work through illness

explanation.definitionFit: A roster of staff off work unwell is a register of ailing people, each one a patient.

clue.text: If It's not all he has

definitions.text: If It's not all he has

parts.words: If It's not all he has
parts.note: describes a man who holds only a share of something, not the whole of it

explanation.definitionFit: Someone with only a share in a business or property holds a portion and not the whole.

clue.text: Big lake up country

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name of the country Ireland

explanation.surface: A large lake somewhere in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EIRE (Ireland) backwards, as this is a down entry. Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes, a very large body of fresh water.

clue.text: They are empowered to go over our heads

definitions.text: They are empowered to go over our heads

parts.words: They are empowered to go over our heads
parts.note: sounds like officials with authority to bypass us, but describes powered machines flying overhead

explanation.definitionFit: Planes and helicopters are engine-powered machines that fly above people on the ground.

clue.text: Shown to have a deficit and, charged

indicators.note: together with deficit, this says the word for shown is left short of something
a deficit is a shortfall, so one letter is missing from the word

parts.note: shown means indicated, pointed out

explanation.surface: Someone whose accounts revealed a shortfall was then prosecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have a deficit' reads as being in debt, but it says INDICATED lacks an A.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally accused of a crime, as a prosecutor charges a suspect.

clue.text: She's possibly recalled in a famous children's story

definitions.text: She's possibly recalled in a famous children's story

indicators.note: possibly says the following letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A heroine half-remembered from a well-known nursery tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RECALLEDIN, and the whole clue also describes the girl of the fairy tale with the glass slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the pantomime and fairy tale is a girl in a well-loved tale for young readers.

clue.text: Get involved with an intermediary

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Getting mixed up with a go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between who acts on someone else's behalf, as a sales representative does.

clue.text: Holding up catch on a York- shire river

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the word for catch so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: to net is to catch
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: Lifting a fish out of a river in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the net upside down in this down entry, giving TEN. The Ure flows through the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of a property or post, the possession of it for a term.

clue.text: Evidence of spiritual strength

definitions.meaning: facts that establish something is true
the alcoholic strength of spirits, as in 70 degrees

explanation.surface: Signs of religious fortitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that settles a question, and also the measure of alcohol strength in spirits.

clue.text: Naval vessel which should' be quarantined?

definitions.meaning: a ship of the navy carrying aircraft
someone harbouring a disease who passes it to others

explanation.surface: A warship that ought to be held in isolation.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship that launches aircraft, and also a person who spreads an infection and so ought to be isolated.

clue.text: Prison for a debt-collector-who has gone wrong

parts.note: to dun is to press for payment, so a dun is a debt-collector

indicators.note: gone wrong suggests the following letters have been put out of order

explanation.surface: A jail for a bailiff whose career went off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the word gone into GEON. A dun, from the verb to dun, is a dated word for someone pressing a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark underground cell in a castle, used to lock up captives.

clue.text: Ring the swimming bath back

indicators.note: back says the letters of the word for a swimming bath run in reverse

parts.note: a pool is a swimming bath

explanation.surface: Phoning the local baths in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns POOL around. 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the noun for a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed curve, as a hoop or circle is.

clue.text: Pass by city and town

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
Chester is a city in Cheshire, north-west England

explanation.surface: Travelling past a city on the way to a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Colchester is a town in Essex, England, and Chester a cathedral city in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Colchester is an English settlement in Essex, often called Britain's oldest recorded one.

clue.text: Bet it's the wife!

parts.note: the word bet is the first half of the word better, and the phrase for that is a name for one's spouse

explanation.definitionFit: A humorous name a husband uses for his spouse, the superior partner.

clue.text: Given hot tips at the barbers?

definitions.text: Given hot tips at the barbers?

parts.words: Given hot tips at the barbers?
parts.note: hot tips sounds like betting advice, but means hair ends burned with a taper

explanation.definitionFit: Barbers once burned the ends of the hair with a flame, scorching them.

clue.text: An improvement in relations

parts.note: an easing of tension, especially between rival nations

explanation.definitionFit: A French word for the relaxing of hostility between states, used of the Cold War.

clue.text: Agree to a wage cut and drown one's sorrows

explanation.surface: A worker accepts reduced pay and heads for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting lower pay means accepting a fall, and having a drink to forget troubles means a swig of liquor.

clue.text: A cooked -meal served in prison

definitions.meaning: a breakfast dish of oats boiled in water or milk
time served as a jail sentence, British slang

explanation.surface: Breakfast dished up to inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing porridge' is British slang for serving a jail sentence; 'served' moves from dishing up food to serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats boiled in milk or water, and British slang for a stretch behind bars, as in 'doing time'.

clue.text: Revolutionary paper money

parts.note: banknotes issued during the French Revolution, backed by seized church lands

explanation.definitionFit: These were notes printed by the French revolutionary government from 1789.

clue.text: Make no allowance in a speech

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: An address telling listeners there will be no allocation.
explanation.walkthrough: O as a zero means 'no'; RATION follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal address delivered to an audience, such as a funeral eulogy.

clue.text: Putting water into he ship extinguishes the fire

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Flooding the vessel to put out a fire on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container. Slaking is quenching, used of thirst or of fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake is to quench, used of putting out flames as well as thirst.

clue.text: What is wrong in, a record being beaten?

indicators.note: in places the word for wrongdoing inside the word for a record

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Asking what is amiss in a record that has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record being beaten' suggests a sporting best, but 'being beaten' is the definition, and 'a record' is a ship's log.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defeated, as a side going down in a match.

clue.text: Implying that women are second rate at bridge?

definitions.text: Implying that women are second rate at bridge?

parts.words: Implying that women are second rate at bridge?
parts.note: a sign saying only males play here, read as a slight on female card players

explanation.definitionFit: A sign like 'Men at work' read as limiting a card table to males suggests they play the better game.

clue.text: House calls may double. -a' salesman's objective

indicators.note: doubling a word means writing it twice in succession

parts.note: a salesman aims to get an order

explanation.surface: Door-to-door callers hope to double their sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may double' writes ORDER twice. The Speaker of the House of Commons calls 'Order, order!' to quiet MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker's cry to restore quiet in the Commons is a familiar parliamentary call.

clue.text: Gloomy doctor has a listener

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A depressed physician has someone to confide in.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for dismal or bleak.

clue.text: Transport will be back at-: eleven

indicators.note: back means the little word at is written in reverse

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a team of eleven in cricket

explanation.surface: Getting home by quarter to eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word at around, giving TA. XI is also a cricket or football team of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car for getting about town.

clue.text: A shade depressed

explanation.surface: Something a bit downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is a colour, and feeling low is having the blues.

clue.text: Anger with territory is* nothing new to it

definitions.text: Anger with territory is* nothing new to it

parts.note: ire means anger
land is territory

explanation.surface: A country long used to disputes over borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a country with a long history of conflict over territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The island nation has a long history of partition and dispute over land.

clue.text: A new role in flight-control

indicators.note: new suggests the letters around it are made fresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A new job in aviation management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROLEIN into ILERON, after A. 'flight-control' is the definition: an aileron controls an aircraft's roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap on an aeroplane's wing that controls its roll.

clue.text: Animals unlikely to be overlooked

parts.note: overlooked as looked over from above: these creatures are too tall to be seen over

explanation.definitionFit: These long-necked African beasts are the tallest land mammals, so little peers down on them.

clue.text: He has absolute control of the French vessel

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone who runs the French kitchen with an iron fist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules with unchecked power.
